item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Ritu studies the diagram of right-angled triangles $PQR$ and $XYZ$, each with a right angle marked. The hypotenuses $QR$ and $YZ$ are equal, and legs $PQ$ and $XY$ are equal.

Which claim correctly decides congruence?

options.A: Call the triangles congruent even when either triangle need not be right-angled.
options.B: Say the same RHS match also settles congruence for non-right SSA pairs in general.
options.C: The triangles are congruent by RHS: right angle, equal hypotenuses, and one equal corresponding leg.
options.D: Require two equal angles and the included side (ASA) before congruence can be decided here.
